request.task: Generate the original-target case set using this schema. Use only the documented project adapter vocabulary.

profile.subject: SeasonSwitch
constraints: state is static: reset it to OFF before every case, or test order decides results
never start either javax.swing.Timer; call timerOff() directly
capture System.out; most outcomes are only observable as printed text
drive state through the public API, never by assigning `state`; the current State-pattern refactor retains a compatibility int field, but tests must not depend on assigning it

context.case_vocabulary:
# SeasonSwitch JUnit case vocabulary (generate and adapt modes)

The shared test-case schemas intentionally leave `setup`, `inputs`, and `expected` open.
For SeasonSwitch, the project adapter uses the following vocabulary. P1 should
emit cases using these keys; unfamiliar fields fail validation instead of being ignored.

| Field | Used in | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | `setup`, `expected` | `"OFF"`, `"COOL"`, `"HEAT"` | Current mode |
| `room.temp` | `setup` | integer | Room temperature before action |
| `ac.isOn` | `setup`, `expected` | boolean | Air-conditioner switch |
| `heater.isOn` | `setup`, `expected` | boolean | Heater switch |
| `stdout` | `expected` | string | Exact output from the invoked method, with `\n` newlines |

`inputs` must be `{}`: `cool`, `heat`, `off`, and `timerOff` take no arguments.
Missing `setup.state` means starting in OFF mode. At least one assertion is required.
State is reached using `cool()`, `heat()`, or `off()`, not by assigning `SeasonSwitch.state`.
The adapter stops Swing timers during testing, and captures only the output of
**the unit under test**, not setup transitions.

Example case (illustrative only; not a real EP agent output):

```json
{
  "id": "BVA-01",
  "method": "BVA",
  "target": "original",
  "unit": "timerOff",
  "setup": {"state": "COOL", "room.temp": 68},
  "inputs": {},
  "expected": {"state": "COOL", "ac.isOn": false, "stdout": "Cooling stopped. RmTemp=68\n"},
  "partition": "coolTemp-at",
  "rationale": "At 68, room.temp > coolTemp is false"
}
```

The materializer checks the existing G1 decision **against the original case-set bytes**.
In `--mode adapt`, it copies the approved cases, changes only the `target` label
in memory, and renders a test class that runs against Maven's `refactored` profile.
The expected values, preconditions, case IDs, and units are unchanged. Its output
is Java source only; it does not modify `testcases_final.json` or write a second
case-set JSON. A separate LangGraph G3 approval is still required before executing
tests against the refactored source in the full workflow. The `adapt` CLI itself
does not implement G3 or run Maven.

Example (from the repository root, after a real G1 acceptance):

```bash
python3 .agents/testgen/materialize_junit.py \
  --mode adapt \
  --profile projects/seasonswitch/profile.json \
  --cases runs/<run>/testcases_final.json \
  --report runs/<run>/dedupe-report.md \
  --log runs/<run>/hitl_decisions.json \
  --out java/src/test/java/cse4392/SeasonSwitchAdaptedTest.java
```

If the original generated class is already present, this adds a second JUnit
class rather than replacing it. Loc's harness instead reuses the original Java
tests and swaps Maven profiles, which is sufficient while the public interface
remains compatible. This adapter is project-specific; the main testgen CLI
contains no SeasonSwitch behavior.

schema.title: A set of SeasonSwitch test cases

items.title: Project-agnostic test case
items.description: One executable case for any unit under test. setup/inputs/expected are free-form objects whose vocabulary is defined by the project profile at projects/<project>/profile.json -- that is what keeps this schema usable for a stateless function and a stateful object alike.

unit.description: The unit under test, matching a name in the profile's `units`.

setup.description: Preconditions established before the call. Empty for a stateless unit.

inputs.description: Arguments passed to the unit. Empty when it takes none.

expected.description: Every observable outcome the profile declares: return value, state variables, output, or exception.

partition.description: Name of the equivalence class or boundary side this case represents.

rationale.description: Why this case represents that class and no other.

skill:
---
id: bva-tests
order: 11
executor: agent
inputs: [projects/<project>/profile.json]
outputs: [testcases_bva.json]
gate: none
schema: schemas/testcase-set.schema.json
---

# Purpose
Derive boundary-value-analysis test cases for any unit under test. Boundaries come from the profile,
not from this file.

# Methodology
Read `.agents/_methodology/boundary-value-analysis.md` and apply it in full — its point selection,
robust-vs-normal rule, and decision-embedded-threshold rule are authoritative for how cases are
derived.

# Contract
- Reads: `projects/<project>/profile.json`, the source at `profile.source`, and the methodology
  file above.
- Writes: `testcases_bva.json` matching `schemas/testcase-set.schema.json`.
- Runs as a subagent alongside `ep-tests`; the parent `testgen` launches both concurrently and
  neither may read the other's output.
- For every boundary emit the value below, on, and above. No interior representatives.

# Procedure
1. Read `boundaries` from the profile. Each entry gives a `value`, the `applies_to` unit, and the
   `condition` that decides the branch.
2. For each boundary emit three cases: `value - 1`, `value`, `value + 1` (methodology §Method 1;
   add the just-invalid side only when validation is specified — §Method 2).
3. Derive the expected outcome from `on_true` / `on_false` and the condition, not from guessing.
4. **Check the operator.** A `>` boundary and a `<` boundary put the "on" outcome on opposite
   sides, and at the value itself both conditions are false. Assuming all thresholds behave the
   same way produces wrong tests and leaves a branch uncovered.
5. Boundaries that apply to different units or different state dimensions produce different
   classes — do not merge them. When the unit reads `state_variables`, each (state x boundary
   side) combination is its own case.
6. `rationale` names the boundary and which side the value sits on: `below`, `at`, `above`.
   `partition` is `<boundary>-<side>`.
7. Honour every entry in `constraints` when constructing `setup`.

# Output shape
`{"generated_by": "bva-tests", "target": <target>, "cases": [...]}` — each case has `id`
(`BVA-NN`), `method` `"BVA"`, `target`, `unit`, `setup`, `inputs`, `expected`, `partition`,
`rationale`. Assert every `observable` key the case can reach — printed text and device state can
disagree if the implementation is wrong.

# Self-check before finishing
Run the methodology file's checklist, plus:
- [ ] >=3 cases per `boundaries` entry (below, at, above — smallest domain step)
- [ ] both sides of every cut tested, correct side keyed to the operator
- [ ] no two cases share all `dedupe_key` fields
- [ ] every `constraints` entry honoured
- [ ] file validates against `schemas/testcase-set.schema.json`
